title: Success Criteria: Deciding What Good Means
summary: Before you can improve an LLM feature you have to say, in numbers, what success looks like. This lesson turns fuzzy goals into criteria, metrics and thresholds you can test against.
objectives: Turn a vague product goal into specific, measurable criteria with pass thresholds
Compute precision, recall, F1 and F-beta from a confusion matrix and explain when accuracy misleads
Choose an operating threshold by weighing the cost of false positives against false negatives
Size an evaluation set from the margin of error you can tolerate
Recognise when a metric has stopped tracking what users care about (Goodhart's law)
prerequisites: Comfort with fractions, percentages and averages. It helps to have built or used an LLM feature, for example from [Anatomy of a Prompt](/learn/prompt-and-context/prompt-anatomy), but no statistics background is assumed.
